'''Tenno Shrine''' (天皇神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Shiga|af|Shiga-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Shiga|ar|شيغا (محافظة)|az|Şiqa prefekturası|azb|شیقا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Shiga|be|Сіга (прэфектура)|bg|Шига|bn|শিগা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|br|Prefedelezh Shiga|ca|Prefectura de Shiga|cdo|Shiga-gâing|ce|Сига (префектура)|ceb|Shiga-ken|ckb|پارێزگای شیگا|cs|Prefektura Šiga|cy|Shiga (talaith)|da|Shiga-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Shiga|eo|Gubernio Ŝiga|es|Prefectura de Shiga|et|Shiga prefektuur|eu|Shiga (prefektura)|fa|استان شیگا|fi|Shigan prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Shiga|frr|Shiga (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Shiga|gl|Prefectura de Shiga|hak|Shiga-yen|he|שיגה (מחוז)|hr|Shiga (prefektura)|hu|Siga prefektúra|hy|Սիգա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Shiga|ilo|Prepektura ti Shiga|it|Prefettura di Shiga|ja|滋賀県|jv|Préfèktur Shiga|ka|სიგის პრეფექტურა|ko|시가현|la|Shigaënsis|lt|Šigos prefektūra|lv|Sigas prefektūra|mk|Шига (префектура)|mn|Шига муж|mni|ꯁꯤꯒꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|शिगा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Shiga|ne|सिगा|nl|Shiga (prefectuur)|no|Shiga (prefektur)|os|Сигæ|pl|Prefektura Shiga|pnb|ضلع شیگا|pt|Shiga|ro|Prefectura Shiga|ru|Сига|sco|Shiga Prefectur|se|Shiga prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Shiga|si|ෂිගා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Shiga Prefecture|sk|Šiga (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Шига|su|Préféktur Shiga|sv|Shiga prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Shiga|tg|Устони Шига|th|จังหวัดชิงะ|tl|Prepektura ng Shiga|tr|Shiga|tt|Сига (префектура)|uk|Префектура Сіґа|ur|شیگا پریفیکچر|vi|Shiga|war|Shiga (prefektura)|wuu|滋贺县|zh|滋贺县|zh_classical|滋賀縣|zh_min_nan|Siga-koān|zh_yue|滋賀縣|qid=Q131358|lt=Shiga Prefecture}}{{ill|Ōtsu|en|Ōtsu|qid=Q202907|lt=Otsu City}}.

== Geography ==
{{ill|West Japan Railway Company|arz|شركة سكك حديد غرب اليابان|azb|باتی ژاپون دمیریول‌لاری|ca|Companyia de Ferrocarrils del Japó Occidental|cs|JR West|da|West Japan Railway Company|de|West Japan Railway Company|eo|JR Okcidenta|es|West Japan Railway Company|fa|شرکت راه‌آهن غرب ژاپن|fi|JR Nishi-Nihon|fr|West Japan Railway Company|hu|West Japan Railway Company|id|Perusahaan Kereta Api Jepang Barat|it|West Japan Railway Company|ja|西日本旅客鉄道|jv|West Japan Railway Company|ko|서일본 여객철도|ms|Syarikat Kereta Api Jepun Barat|nds|JR Westjapan|nl|West Japan Railway Company|pl|West Japan Railway Company|pt|West Japan Railway Company|ru|West Japan Railway Company|sv|JR Nishi Nihon|th|บริษัทรถไฟญี่ปุ่นตะวันตก|tl|West Japan Railway Company|tr|West Japan Railway Company|uk|West Japan Railway Company|ur|ویسٹ جاپان ریلوے کمپنی|wuu|西日本旅客铁道|zh|西日本旅客鐵道|zh_min_nan|Se Ji̍t-pún Lú-kheh Thih-tō|zh_yue|西日本旅客鐵道|qid=Q502125|lt=JR}}{{ill|Wani Station|en|Wani Station|qid=Q5365302|lt=Wani Station}} is located approximately 1.1 {{ill|Kilometre|en|Kilometre|qid=Q828224|lt=kilometer}} to the southwest <ref name=":0">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.biwako-visitors.jp/spot/detail/158|title=天皇神社{{!}}滋賀県観光情報|accessdate=2020-04-22|publisher=びわこビジターズビューロー|date=2015-06-23}}</ref>, and a 10‐minute walk away <ref name=":1">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://nishioumi.ct-net.com/00-05.shtml|title=歴史散歩・和邇天皇神社　和邇祭り|accessdate=2020-04-22|publisher=京都新聞西近江販売所連合|year=2000|month=05}}</ref>. It is situated along the roadside of Ryūka Crossing (present‐day {{ill|Shiga Prefectural Road Route 311|ja|滋賀県道311号途中志賀線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiga Prefecture Route 311, Tokochu Shiga Line|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11564859}}) {{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=20}}. It is about 5 minutes from {{ill|Lake Biwa west running through road|ja|湖西道路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kosai Road|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 琵琶湖西縦貫道路|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11573837}} ({{ill|Japan National Route 161|en|Japan National Route 161|qid=Q11421413|lt=National Route 161}}) {{ill|Wani interchange|ja|和迩インターチェンジ|lt=Wani IC|lt_ja=和邇IC|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani IC|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418218}} <ref name=":2">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://otsu.or.jp/thingstodo/spot213|title=天皇神社|accessdate=2020-04-22|publisher=びわ湖大津観光協会}}</ref>.

== History ==
In 966 ({{ill|Kōhō|en|Kōhō|qid=Q1327182|lt=Kōhō}} 3) the Gozu Tennō of {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|en|Yasaka Shrine|qid=Q692714|lt=Yasaka Shrine}} was returned, and it is said that it began under the name "Wani Gozu Tennōsha" {{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=20}}. The enshrinement is said to have been established in the late {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura}} <ref name=":0" />. In 1876 ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 9) it acquired its current name {{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=20}}. At that time, it became a village shrine <ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=118|title=神社紹介　天皇神社（テンノウジンジャ）|accessdate=2020-04-22|publisher=滋賀県神社庁}}</ref>.

== Shrine Grounds ==
The main hall was constructed in {{ill|1324|en|1324|qid=Q5773|lt=1324}} (the first year of {{ill|Shōchū (era)|en|Shōchū (era)|qid=Q1327153|lt=Shōchū}}) and has been designated as an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} {{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=20}}. This main hall is one of only three examples of {{ill|Kirizuma-style|ja|切妻造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gabled Roof Construction|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q13308575}} in Shiga Prefecture (the others can be seen at {{ill|Ono Takamura Shrine|ja|小野篁神社}} and {{ill|Ono Dōfū Shrine|ja|小野道風神社}}) <ref name=":0" />. The format of having three main halls with a rear worship space in a gabled structure is rare nationwide <ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www5.city.otsu.shiga.jp/kankyou/content.asp?key=0401000000&skey=207|title=大津のかんきょう宝箱　天皇神社（和邇中）|accessdate=2020-04-22|publisher=大津市環境部環境政策課}}</ref>. A characteristic feature from the time of its establishment is the remaining outline of a {{ill|kaerumata|ja|蟇股|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toad‐leg Motif|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q123117911}} <ref name=":0" />. The roof is made of {{ill|cypress bark roof|ja|檜皮葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cypress Bark Roofing|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q90373477}} <ref name=":2" />.

== Annual Festival ==
The annual festival of Tenno Shrine, known as "Wani Festival" and sometimes referred to as "Goka Festival" <ref name=":1" />, is held by shrine officials from the Wani‐naka area and the districts of {{ill|Q11408105|ja|南浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minamihama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11408105}}, {{ill|Q16283273|ja|中浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q16283273}}, {{ill|Kitahama|ja|北浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitahama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11402355}}, {{ill|Q11376872|ja|今宿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imaju|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11376872}}, and {{ill|Q11669044|ja|高城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11669044}} <ref name=":1" />. In the Minamihama district, on the early morning of the festival day, shrine officials depart from {{ill|Kimoto Shrine|ja|木元神社}} to Tenno Shrine, and in the afternoon, portable shrines from other regions proceed to the lakeside resting area <ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.rekihaku.otsu.shiga.jp/db/jiten/data/245.html|title=和邇祭{{!}}歴史事典|accessdate=2020-04-22|publisher=大津市歴史博物館}}</ref>. Its origin is attributed to the incident during {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|qid=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}}'s assault on {{ill|Mount Hiei Arson (1571)|ja|比叡山焼き討ち (1571st year )|lt=Mount Hiei Arson}}, when the portable shrine of {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi Taisha|qid=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Taisha}} fled to Tenno Shrine, which subsequently led to conflicts over its return <ref name=":1" />. It was once held annually on May 8, but nowadays, due to holiday scheduling, it is observed on the second Sunday of May each year <ref name=":1" />.
